name: oneiq
description: Ask plain-language questions about your VMs, hosts, storage, cloud costs and sizing, answered live from your OneIQ data.

interface.longDescription:
OneIQ brings your IT infrastructure data into ChatGPT. Connect your OneIQ account and ask plain-language questions about the environments OneIQ has collected from your data centres and clouds — VMware, Hyper-V, Nutanix, Kubernetes, AWS and Azure. Find out how many VMs you run and where, which hosts are busiest, how storage and CPU are used, and what your infrastructure costs.

What you can do:
• List the OneIQ data sources you have access to and see what each one contains.
• Ask questions like "How many VMs are powered on?" or "Which ten hosts had the highest P95 CPU last month?" — OneIQ turns the question into a query and returns the answer from your own data.
• Look up processor and cloud instance specifications, list prices and exchange rates from OneIQ's reference catalogue.
• Get right-sized AWS or Azure instance recommendations for a workload, with monthly and multi-year cost.
• Flag an incorrect or empty answer to the OneIQ team directly from the chat.

All tools read data you already have permission to see in OneIQ; nothing in your environment is changed. Requires a OneIQ account.
defaultPrompt: How many virtual machines are in my environment, and how many are powered on?
Which 10 hosts had the highest 95th-percentile CPU utilization over the last 30 days?
Compare the monthly cost of running 8 vCPUs and 32 GB on AWS versus Azure.

positive.description: Discover the catalogue of data sources the account can see.
positive.prompt: What OneIQ data sources can you see?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a table of data sources (Name, Id, Type, Status, Data from, Data to) for the test account, including the demo data source MyWorkspace.

positive.description: Simple inventory question against the demo data source.
positive.prompt: In the MyWorkspace data source, how many virtual machines are there and how many are powered on?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves MyWorkspace to its id, runs a query and returns the VM count and powered-on count, with the generated query and the time window covered.

positive.description: Utilisation question with an explicit statistic and window.
positive.prompt: For MyWorkspace, what is the 95th percentile CPU utilization of the top 10 hosts over the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a ranked table of hosts by P95 CPU, restating the statistic and window, and notes the data range the source holds.

positive.description: Reference lookup that must not use the customer's estate data.
positive.prompt: What does an AWS m6i.2xlarge cost per month in us-east-1, in USD?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the instance specification and list price from OneIQ's reference catalogue, without querying any data source.

positive.prompt: Recommend an AWS instance in us-east-1 for a workload needing 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory, and show the cost.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns an AWS design header for us-east-1 in USD with a Configuration line, a multi-year total, an approximate monthly figure and cost line items, and states that the sizing is compute-only.

negative.description: General knowledge question — the plugin should not be invoked.
negative.prompt: Explain the differences between vSphere and Proxmox.

negative.description: Code generation naming a cloud instance type — the plugin should not be invoked.
negative.prompt: Write Terraform to launch an m6i.2xlarge instance in us-east-1.

negative.description: Analysis of data supplied in the chat rather than in a OneIQ data source — the plugin should not be invoked.
negative.prompt: Summarise this VM spreadsheet I uploaded.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. Read-only access to your OneIQ data sources: list the data sources you can see, ask natural-language questions about your infrastructure inventory and performance, look up processor and cloud instance specifications and prices, and get AWS/Azure instance sizing recommendations with costs. Includes a report_problem tool that lets you flag an incorrect or empty answer to the OneIQ team; it is the only tool that writes anything, and it only creates a support report.
